SK0281 The attribute promises to set members that do not exist

[SetsRequiredMembers] on a constructor of a type that declares and inherits no required member.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

The attribute is a promise to the compiler — this constructor assigns every required member, so a caller need not use an object initializer. Against an empty set it promises nothing, and it is worse than noise in two directions: it tells a reader that requiredness is in play on this type when it is not, and it keeps compiling silently on the day somebody adds a required member that the constructor does not assign, which is the exact case the attribute exists to make loud. ⚠ Models apply it defensively, because it is the documented way to make a constructor and required coexist and the constructor is the part they were asked for.

⚠ Not hosted, and the zero was measured rather than assumed. Reading IsEnabledByDefault/DefaultSeverity out of SDK 10.0.400's analyzer assemblies gives 442 descriptors and none of them is this shape — an error log could not have answered it, because a Hidden rule and an absent one produce the same empty log. A behavioural probe with all 120 IDE ids and all 320 CA ids forced to warning, EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true, AnalysisMode=All and AnalysisLevel=latest-all reported nothing on a [SetsRequiredMembers] constructor of a type with no required members, on a compilation where IDE0055, IDE0160, IDE0290, IDE0380 and CA1051 all fired and no analyzer crashed. jb inspectcode 2025.2.6 reports it on the same file, and correctly declines the type that does have a required member.

Example

Instead of:

using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;

sealed class Options {
    [SetsRequiredMembers]
    public Options(string path) => Path = path;

    public string Path { get; init; }
}

Write:

sealed class Options {
    public Options(string path) => Path = path;

    public string Path { get; init; }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ The base chain is part of the question, not a refinement of it. [SetsRequiredMembers] covers the required members of the whole hierarchy, so a type with none of its own but a base that has one is doing exactly what the attribute is for. The walk runs to object; stopping at the declared type would have been this rule's worst false positive and there is a fixture for it. ⚠ An error type anywhere in the base chain withdraws the finding. A base class whose reference is missing binds to an error symbol whose member list is empty — indistinguishable from a base with no required members, and every inheriting constructor would become a false positive. ⚠ The attribute's identity is asked, never its name: a SetsRequiredMembersAttribute outside System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis means whatever its author made it mean. ⚠ The deleted span is the whole attribute list when this is its only attribute and the attribute plus a separating comma when it is not — [] and [A, ] are both parse errors, and a fix whose output does not parse means SK9099 refuses to write the file.
